# Unit-test generator: how to work on it

Repository layout: the application is in `Source/UnitTestGenerator`, BaseAgent in `Source/BaseAgent`,
the tests and pilots in `Test`, the requirements and other documents in `Docs`.

The requirements are the contract: [unittest_generator_requirments.txt](../../../Docs/unittest_generator_requirments.txt).
It is the only requirements file; never create dated copies of it.
The agent flow is drawn in [ORCHESTRATION.md](../../../Docs/ORCHESTRATION.md).

## Rules

1. Requirements first. A change in behaviour is written into the requirements (stable IDs, new IDs
   for new behaviour, gaps are fine) before the code. Every ID cited in code must exist there; the
   test `test_every_cited_requirement_exists` checks it.
2. Few files: one Python file per agent (ARCH-10), contracts in `ut_contracts.py`, orchestration in
   `ut_pipeline.py`, tool provisioning in `ut_setup.py`, one entry file per OS
   (`unittest_generator.bat`, `unittest_generator.sh`), all tests in `Test/test_unittest_generator.py`, pilots in `Test/pilots`.
3. Three layers: brains (Opus, Qwen3 8B) only suggest and are validated (ARCH-5); agents decide;
   tools act. Deterministic extraction before any LLM (ARCH-6). Every brain suggestion gets a
   deterministic check before it is used (A1-PL4, A3-BD12, A4-23g); evidence the brain linked to a
   function never justifies a source fix (A1-PL13, A4-23i).
4. Tools come only from `tools/toolchain.json`, written by `ut_setup.py` (TP-10), git included. Never
   add a tool search or a fallback compiler to an agent; extend `ut_setup.py` and its pins in
   `ut_config.json` (official release page, version, SHA-256) instead (TP-4).
5. Agents never call each other; the orchestrator is the only MCP client (ORC-1, ORC-2). Every handoff
   is a contract from `ut_contracts.py`, bound to the SUT and test-suite signatures (ORC-10).
6. Never weaken a test to make it pass (A3-85a); never change production code without a classified
   source defect, two independent evidence items (A4-23f), Agent3's reverification and a clean
   static-analyzer comparison (A4-32a). A source fix reaches the tested branch only through the
   review pull request (ORC-25, A4-23c); in a local folder only on a separate branch.
7. Never overwrite a file of the user's repository that the pipeline did not write or that was
   edited (ORC-14, ORC-14a). Never force-push, rewrite history, or delete or rename a branch (ORC-31).
   Credentials are never written anywhere (ORC-21).
8. Fully automatic except one step: a person reviews production-source changes by merging the pull
   request (ORC-9, ORC-26). What cannot be decided is reported.
9. The pipeline's own files from an earlier delivery (marked "generated by agent_unittest_generator")
   are never existing tests, E5 evidence or project stubs.

## Before you finish

- `Source\UnitTestGenerator\unittest_generator.bat test` (Windows) or
  `Source/UnitTestGenerator/unittest_generator.sh test` (Linux): all tests pass.
- Pilots: `pilot-c`, `pilot-cpp`, `pilot-deps`; benchmark: `benchmark` (no false fix, ORC-16).
- For delivery changes: a run with a repository link (the RepositoryTests use a local bare repository).
